clue.text: Scholar revised a manic idea about carbon

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the next piece
a revised text has been reworked, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: An academic rethinks a crazy idea about carbon, perhaps a climate theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges A MANIC IDEA into ACADEMIIAN, and 'about' wraps it round C to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of an academy, especially a learned scholar of standing, is a synonym for a scholar.

clue.text: Church with old Irish singing group

explanation.surface: A church with old Irish singers.
explanation.definitionFit: An organised body of singers, usually performing in church, is a singing group.

clue.text: Expert fish worker

parts.note: a dab is a small flatfish
a hand is a manual worker, as on a farm or ship

explanation.surface: A skilled worker in the fishing trade.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal British idiom for someone highly skilled at something, so an expert.

clue.text: Musician Mike strangely silent around king

parts.note: M is Mike in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: around puts the shuffled letters on either side of the next piece
strangely says the letters of silent appear in an odd order

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A musician named Mike oddly falls silent near a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges SILENT into INSTEL; 'around' wraps it round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval singer or musician who performed at court, a travelling entertainer.

clue.text: Small measure needed to rein in a cleric

indicators.note: to rein in is to hold inside, so the letter goes into the measure

parts.note: 1mm, one millimetre, is a small measure, the digit 1 read as letter I

explanation.surface: A small step is needed to restrain a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 1mm is read as IMM, the figure one looking like the letter I; 'to rein in' puts A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A Muslim prayer leader of a mosque, so a cleric in Islam.

clue.text: Shot prior to retirement?

parts.note: the shot is a drink and retirement is going to bed, not leaving work or being fired

explanation.surface: A gunshot or sporting shot just before someone retires from their career.
explanation.walkthrough: Retirement here is bedtime, and the shot is a small drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcoholic drink taken just before going to bed is the shot before retiring.

clue.text: No more suckers? That's intolerable!

definitions.meaning: if only one drinking tube is left, there are no more after it
the final burden that makes something unbearable, said when patience runs out

explanation.surface: Someone fed up with being fooled says they have had enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suckers' looks like dupes; it means drinking straws, which you suck through.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for the final small burden that breaks one's patience, from the straw that broke the camel's back.

clue.text: Fellowship of real ale fans entertaining a Democrat on lake

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the letter goes inside the society's name

parts.note: CAMRA, the Campaign for Real Ale, is the British society of real ale enthusiasts
Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Beer lovers bond while hosting an American Democrat at a lakeside.
explanation.walkthrough: CAMRA is the Campaign for Real Ale, a British pub-beer group; 'entertaining' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutual trust and friendship among people in a group is a synonym for fellowship.

clue.text: Trump has vehicle in Indiana abandoned

indicators.note: in places the vehicle inside the remaining letters
an abandoned house is emptied, so the word Indiana loses its contents and keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Donald Trump is pictured leaving a car behind in the state of Indiana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' empties Indiana to its outer letters I and A; 'in' puts VAN between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivana Trump, the businesswoman and first wife of Donald Trump, bore the surname as a famous first name.

clue.text: Boss to lead with three articles

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead, from Latin plumbum
an, an and a are three indefinite articles in a row

explanation.surface: A newspaper boss is told to lead with three articles on the front page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' is the metal here, not to go first: its symbol is PB.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal idiom for the most important person in an organisation, the one in charge.

clue.text: Sage Derby perhaps feeding mother

indicators.note: feeding into means going inside, so the hat goes into the word for mother

parts.note: mama is an informal word for mother
a derby is a bowler hat, an example of a hat

explanation.surface: Derby, a sage cheese, is fed to someone's mother.
explanation.walkthrough: Sage Derby is a British cheese marbled with sage, which hides that 'Sage' is the definition and 'Derby' is a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A title given in India to a person revered for great wisdom, as Gandhi was, so a sage.

clue.text: Best players unable to finish meal

parts.note: the cream is the best of anything

indicators.note: a word unable to finish loses its final letter

parts.note: a team is a group of players

explanation.surface: The top sportsmen cannot complete their meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unable to finish' drops the final M from CREAM TEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Afternoon tea with scones, jam and clotted cream is a traditional British light meal.

clue.text: Something wicked and frivolous that helps dispel gloom

parts.note: a candle has a wick, so it is jokingly wicked
light means not serious, frivolous

explanation.surface: Something evil and silly that cheers people up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' means fitted with a wick, not evil.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft light from candles drives away darkness, the gloom of a dim room.

clue.text: Report that might be current?

definitions.meaning: a report or narrative of events
a bank's current ... is one kind, so this is something that might be current

explanation.surface: A news report that may be up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like up-to-date; it points to a bank's current account.
explanation.definitionFit: A description of events is a report, and the banking sense covers current deposits.

clue.text: Some local cut taxes in city once

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A council is cutting some local taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' belongs to the definition: the city once was in India, now renamed Kolkata.
explanation.definitionFit: The former name of Kolkata, the city in West Bengal, India, before its 2001 renaming.

clue.text: One obsessed in new way renouncing whiskey

indicators.note: renouncing means giving up, so the letter is dropped from the word new

parts.note: taken as written
W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Someone obsessed has given up whiskey in a new way of living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renouncing whiskey' takes W out of NEW, leaving NE.
explanation.definitionFit: A geek fixated on one narrow interest, often technical, is the obsessive the clue describes.

clue.text: Unusually good ground yields element

parts.note: rare can mean unusually good, as in a rare treat
earth is ground or soil

explanation.surface: Exceptionally fertile soil gives a good harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the lanthanide metals such as neodymium, each a chemical element.

clue.text: Drink that could make Coppola drunk

indicators.note: drunk means unsteady and muddled, so the director's name is jumbled

explanation.surface: A sweet fizzy drink might get the film director Francis Ford Coppola tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges COPPOLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet bottled drink containing alcohol and resembling a soft drink is a type of drink.

clue.text: Cinema fire — temperature hot inside

indicators.note: inside places the next pieces within the word meaning fire

parts.note: to fire up feelings is to arouse them
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A fire breaks out in a cinema, and it is hot indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' is a verb here, to stir up, not a blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cinema showing independent or foreign films, an arts picture house.

clue.text: Branch in High Street will keep bonnet that's reduced

parts.note: food that is high has gone off

indicators.note: will keep means holds within, so the trimmed bonnet goes inside
reduced says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a hood is a bonnet, as on a car or as headwear

explanation.surface: A shop in the high street sells off a bonnet at a reduced price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High Street' looks like one place, but 'High' means rotten, as food that has gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: A side shoot of a plant or a subsidiary of an organisation, so a branch.

clue.text: Female on farm by river delivers pitcher

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep on a farm

explanation.surface: A farm woman by a river brings a jug of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A large wide-mouthed jug for water, as once used with a washbasin, is a pitcher.

clue.text: Key often used by news boss went in

parts.note: Enter is a much-used key on a computer keyboard
ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A news editor types and hits a much-used key.
explanation.definitionFit: To come or go into a place is to have entered it, the past tense matching went in.

clue.text: Negative piece with slogan Reaganites used?

definitions.meaning: a negatively charged particle, a small piece of the atom
Reagan's supporters might have urged voters to ..., a call to vote for Ronald Reagan

explanation.surface: A campaign piece attacks a rival using Reagan's slogans.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as ELECT RON, a plausible campaign call for Ronald Reagan.
explanation.definitionFit: A subatomic particle carrying a negative electric charge, the negative piece of an atom.

clue.text: Trial by TV in the birthplace of science?

parts.note: a trial is a test
the tube is informal for a television set

explanation.surface: A trial by television is held in the place where science began.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on test-tube babies: the glassware is where science, not nature, brings life about.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass laboratory tube, used in IVF, so jokingly where a baby made by science is born.

clue.text: Port Arabs rebuilt

indicators.note: rebuilt means reconstructed in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Arab people reconstruct a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq's main port city on the Shatt al-Arab waterway is an example of a port.

clue.text: Chap's name is love

parts.note: to adore is to love

explanation.surface: A man announces that his name is Love.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's given name, a variant of Isidore, so a chap's name.

clue.text: Nobleman almost skinned?

indicators.note: skinned means the outer layer is stripped, so the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: nearly means almost

explanation.surface: A peer has nearly been flayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinned' strips N and Y from NEARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A British peer ranking above viscount and below marquess, a nobleman.

clue.text: Racing ace, forced out, not best pleased

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace

indicators.note: forced means wrenched out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: cross means annoyed, not best pleased

explanation.surface: A star racing driver forced out of a race is annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forced' rearranges OUT into UTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A form of motor racing on a rough grass or dirt circuit, so a kind of racing.

clue.text: Can't stand, as the drunk

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone unable to stand up, like the drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can't stand' reads as legless; it means dislikes. 'drunk' rearranges AS THE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be unable to bear something means to detest it, an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: Bloke in forces set landmine off

indicators.note: off means going wrong, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A soldier sets off a landmine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SET LANDMINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier of any rank below officer, a military man in the ranks.
